evidence: All incoming branches converge on restoring X, Y, A, and returning with RTI.
The NMI masks an index to 0-3, loads one of four values, and writes it to the CNROM cartridge range.
The routine resets the PPU latch through PPU_STATUS and performs the two required PPU_SCROLL writes.
The routine marks a context active, resets its SP, copies an entry return address onto that stack, and selects it when requested.
The loop rotates one set bit to the requested thread index before ORing ActiveThreadMask.
The loop copies exactly two entry-address bytes to the selected hardware-stack partition.
The routine saves SP by ThreadIndex, advances the index modulo eight, restores the selected SP, and returns into that context.
This block loads the selected context's saved stack pointer and executes TXS.
All StartThread completion paths converge here to set carry and return.
The routine resets a context SP, installs IdleThreadLoop as its return target, and clears its active-mask bit.
The current-context-only stack restoration is skipped here before clearing the requested context's mask bit.
The loop rotates a zero through $FF to clear exactly one ActiveThreadMask bit.
Stopped and initially unused stack partitions return here and repeatedly yield through SwitchThreads.
StartThread and StopThread copy one of eight page-one stack offsets from this table into ThreadStackPointers.
StartThread indexes this split set of per-context base pointers and adds twice the encoded entry selector.
Reset polls PPU_STATUS until its vblank flag becomes set.
A second consecutive PPU_STATUS polling loop waits for the next vblank before RAM initialization.
The outer loop selects descending internal-RAM pages through the high pointer byte.
The inner loop stores zero through an indirect pointer while decrementing the page offset.
The loop writes offscreen Y value $F8 to every fourth byte of OAM page $02.
Reset enables NMI immediately before this loop and waits until a counter reaches two.
The loop writes a CNROM bank value in cartridge space and probes CHR through PPU_DATA until the expected bank-visible byte changes.
The loop compares four ROM signature bytes with internal RAM $07F0-$07F3.
A signature mismatch enters the block that copies the signature and default state into internal RAM.
The four-iteration loop copies StartupWarmBootSignature to WarmBootSignature.
The eight-iteration loop copies StartupWarmBootDefaultState to WarmBootDefaultState.
This block seeds the eight stack partitions and constructs idle return frames before calling StartThread.
The loop stores stack offsets separated by $20 bytes in ThreadStackPointers.
The loop writes IdleThreadLoop minus one as an RTS return address into unused stack partitions.
This outer loop scans four pending start bytes and yields through SwitchThreads between passes.
A nonzero pending value is cleared and passed directly to StartThread.
The block decrements the pending-thread index and continues the four-entry scan.
Reset loads this byte and writes it back to its cartridge address immediately before probing CHR through the PPU.
Reset compares these four bytes with WarmBootSignature and restores them after a mismatch.
Reset copies these eight bytes to WarmBootDefaultState after a signature mismatch.
Reset calls the routine with PPU bases $2000 and $2800; it writes blank tile $24 followed by zero attributes.
The nested loop writes blank tile $24 to PPU_DATA.
The final 64-byte loop writes zero to PPU_DATA after the tile fill.
Scheduler code $30 selects context 3 entry 0; its stored RTS address is $9FFF, so execution begins at $A000.
The routine repeatedly invokes gameplay services, yields four times through SwitchThreads, handles FairiesQueued, and jumps back to $A000.
Both branches that skip or finish queued-fairy handling converge here before the unconditional jump to MainGameplayThread.
Bisqwit's map identifies this entry as DecrementTimer.
The routine consumes TimerUpdateCount and performs decimal subtraction over TimerDigit10 through TimerDigit10000.
NextTimerTick branches here while the copied TimerUpdateCount remains nonzero.
Bisqwit's map identifies this secondary entry as DecrementTimerByOne.
The code advances from TimerFraction to TimerDigit10 and subtracts the configured step.
The loop advances to the next decimal digit and subtracts the outstanding borrow with SBC #$00.
An underflowed decimal digit is wrapped by adding ten before borrow propagation continues.
The loop writes zero to the three lower timer digit addresses $0438-$043A.
The block stores the changed digit and sets bit 7 of TimerDecrementStep as a display-dirty flag.
The block decrements the pending tick counter and loops while more timer updates remain.
When the dirty bit is set and no PPU stream is pending, the block invokes the timer-display builder at $A238.
The block compares the two high decimal digits against one of four thresholds and tests warning-state bit $10.
This threshold branch queues the alternate PPU stream and subsequently clears warning-state bit $10.
Both warning-exit variants converge here with a selected queue value before calling the queue helper at $8E8D.
Both threshold transition paths converge on storing the updated bit field to TimerWarningState.
All paths that skip or complete threshold handling return through this RTS.
The routine copies the four timer digits into the NMI-consumed RAM update buffer and publishes that buffer through $8EA0.
The three-iteration loop copies TimerDisplayWriterCallTemplate to the start of TimerDisplayUpdateBuffer.
The loop copies TimerDigit10000 through TimerDigit10 into ascending display-buffer positions while ORing all digits.
The loop replaces leading zero digits with blank tile $24 and stops at the first nonzero digit.
All display-builder paths tail-call $8EA0, whose instruction flow points the shared PPU stream at RAM $03E6.
BuildTimerDisplayUpdate copies these exact three bytes to RAM; they encode JSR $4469 at the head of the generated update program.
Bisqwit's map identifies this entry as UpdateEnemiesMovement.
The routine consumes the shared update count and advances active records selected through the 17 enemy pointer-table entries.
